title: Analytics pipeline: granular retention policies + legal-hold-safe deletion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement per-tenant, per-event-class retention windows for usage analytics and a legal-hold-safe deletion flow that guarantees auditability, downstream propagation, and minimal service disruption.

Background: current analytics pipeline compacts events at fixed retention boundaries and supports bulk erasure jobs, but we lack: (1) fine-grained retention tied to event class (e.g., debug traces vs billing events), (2) legal hold markers that prevent physical deletion while preserving queryability for audits, and (3) automated propagation of deletions/tombstones to dependent systems (observability index, billing exports, BigQuery snapshots). Customers in regulated industries and our enterprise contracts require defensible legal-hold and provable-deletion capabilities.

Scope and non-goals: this ticket covers backend pipeline changes only (ingestion metadata, retention controller, tombstone markers, downstream notifier). It does NOT include Console UI for configuring retention windows (tracked in PM-428) or on-prem installer changes for air-gapped customers (separate Private workstream).

Design decisions and approach:
- Retention model: attach a retention_class string to every analytics event at ingest (values: ephemeral, standard, billing, pii_sensitive). Default mapping based on ingestion source and schema. Retention windows are evaluated per-tenant + retention_class.
- Legal hold: introduce a durable legal_hold flag on tenant metadata. When set, events in that tenant are excluded from physical deletion and instead transition to a "frozen" state allowing read-only exports. Legal hold changes are recorded in an append-only ledger for auditability.
- Tombstone strategy: logical deletion is implemented via tombstone records written to the same append log with event_id + deletion_reason + initiator + effective_ts. Physical compaction will prune only after retention expiration and legal_hold == false.
- Downstream propagation: implement a deletions topic (Kafka) consumed by downstream sinks (observability indexer, bigquery export job, billing pipeline). Downstream clients must acknowledge and apply deletes or emit compensating records. We'll provide a compatibility shim for existing consumers (see links).
- Backfill and historical enforcement: create a backfill worker that scans compacted partitions to surface items requiring immediate tombstones when retention policy changes shorten windows or legal hold is lifted/added.
- Auditing and exports: add a deletion_audit table (append-only) with cryptographic hash of tombstone payloads for tamper-evidence and create a daily signed snapshot available to compliance teams.

Trade-offs considered:
- Eager physical deletion reduces storage cost but complicates audits; we choose logical tombstones + delayed compaction to favor auditability.
- Per-event retention increases metadata size and slightly increases write path latency; mitigations include encoding retention_class as a small enum and batching retention lookups in the retention controller.
- Full-service blocking on unacknowledged downstream deletes would be brittle; we choose an eventually-consistent model with monitoring and SLA-based compensations.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) schema change at ingest: retention_class enum + event_id normalization (2 days).
2) retention controller service: evaluate TTLs, enqueue tombstones (4 days).
3) deletions topic + consumer shim + downstream integration tests (3 days).
4) backfill worker and one-time migration for tenants with existing long retention flags (3 days).
5) audit snapshot generator + documentation + runbook (2 days).
6) rollout: feature-flagged per-tenant opt-in, shadow run for 2 weeks, then opt-out aggressive pruning only after monitoring SLOs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Missed deletes to downstream sinks: add delivery metrics and alerting, require consumer-ack window of 72h during rollout.
- Storage spike from holding frozen data: impose soft quotas and notify account owners; pursue aggressive compression for frozen partitions.
- Legal hold misuse or accidental toggles: restrict API to SSO+SCIM admins and require two-person approval for removing holds for enterprise tenants.

Next steps and immediate tasks (this ticket):
- Proto: add retention_class enum to analytics ingest proto and update SDKs (ENG).
- Build: retention controller skeleton with in-memory policy evaluator and tombstone writer (ENG).
- Integration: create deletions Kafka topic and consumer shim repository; draft contract for downstream consumers (ENG/Platform).
- Docs: Confluence spec for legal-hold audit workflow and compliance export format (PM/Legal).

Expected deliverables by due_date: retention schema migration, retention controller service in staging, deletions topic + consumer shim, backfill worker PoC, runbook and signed export sample.
acceptance_criteria: Retention_class is present on new analytics events and defaults are documented
Retention controller can produce tombstone records for expired events in staging cluster
Downstream shim consumes deletions topic and tests show deletes applied to observability indexer in staging
Backfill worker can identify candidates and emit tombstones for a sample tenant without data loss
Audit snapshots produced nightly and signed copies stored in secured bucket with access logs
